finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side. The only check is a startsWith('https://') prefix test, so any host, IP, or port is reachable. axios follows redirects by default, which allows https-to-http redirects to internal addresses. The response leaks only its byte length, making this a blind SSRF with a side channel.
finding.source: req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10, parsed by express.json at server.js:5)

trace.note: only validation: typeof string and startsWith('https://'); no host, IP, port, or userinfo check
full attacker string passed to axios.get, which follows redirects by default and does no DNS pinning

finding.guards_checked: Type check (passes any string). Scheme check is a prefix test, not URL parsing. No host/IP allowlist or private/link-local/loopback blocklist. No redirect control (maxRedirects not set, so axios default applies). No DNS pinning or rebinding protection. No auth in this file (depends on any upstream proxy). No timeout or maxContentLength (related DoS, same root cause). No try/catch around await (possible unhandled rejection; Express version not verifiable without package.json).

verdict.guard_found: none. server.js:11 is a typeof check plus a `startsWith("https://")` prefix test, which does not close the finding. No host, IP, or port allowlist exists, and axios.get at server.js:14 has no maxRedirects, beforeRedirect, or lookup restriction.
verdict.reason: req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10, parsed by express.json at server.js:5) is unauthenticated input on POST /profile/avatar, and it reaches axios.get at server.js:14 after only the prefix check at server.js:11, so an attacker can point the server at any https host, including internal ones. The response leaks only img.data.length (server.js:15), which matches the blind side channel described in the claim.
